title: High Quality Genomic DNA Extraction From Fungal Tissue
author: G-Biosciences
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.e6gbhbw
materials: Allow the sample to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Collect and wash fungal tissue
steps.instruction: Collect fungal tissue from liquid culture and wash 2–3 times with sterile water.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K and incubate (optional)
steps.instruction: Add 1 µl Proteinase K solution for every 100 µl Genomic Lysis Buffer, then incubate at 60 °C for 1–2 hours, inverting the tube periodically each hour.

steps.title: Add mycelia to lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add 10–20 mg fungal mycelia to a microcentrifuge tube containing 500 µl Genomic Lysis Buffer.

steps.title: Add grinding resin and homogenize
steps.instruction: Add 30 µl Molecular Grinding Resin™ using wide‑bore pipette tips and grind with a microcentrifuge pestle. For teliospores, add the ground powder to 500 µl Genomic Lysis Buffer and vortex to wet the sample.

steps.title: Add chloroform and mix
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl chloroform and mix by inverting the tube several times.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 14,000 × g, then carefully transfer the upper (aqueous) phase to a clean microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Add DNA Stripping Solution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl DNA Stripping Solution to the sample and invert several times to mix.

steps.title: Incubate at 60 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample for 5–10 minutes at 60 °C.

steps.title: Add Precipitation Solution and check precipitate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl Precipitation Solution and mix by inverting the tube several times. If a white precipitate does not form, add 50 µl aliquots of Precipitation Solution until a white precipitate appears.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µl Precipitation Solution and invert.
If no white precipitate, add 50 µl Precipitation Solution aliquots until precipitate forms.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet precipitate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 14,000 × g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a clean tube, add 500 µl isopropanol, invert the tube 10 times to precipitate DNA, and optionally add 2 µl Mussel Glycogen as a DNA carrier.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl isopropanol and invert 10 times.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14,000 × g for 5 minutes to pellet the genomic DNA.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl 70 % ethanol to the tube and invert several times to wash the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Centrifuge ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 1 minute at 14,000 × g. (The pellet may be hard to see and loosely attached.)

steps.title: Discard ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Decant or pipette off the ethanol wash.

steps.title: Dry pellet by air inversion
steps.instruction: Invert the tube on a clean absorbent surface for several minutes to allow excess ethanol to drain; do not let the pellet dry completely.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in TE Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl TE Buffer to the pellet.

steps.title: Rehydrate DNA at room temperature
steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature for at least 15 minutes to rehydrate the DNA. Incubation at 55–60 °C will speed up rehydration; in that case incubate for 5–60 minutes.

steps.title: Add RNase (optional)
steps.instruction: Add 1 µl LongLife™ RNase for every 100 µl TE Buffer at this stage.

steps.title: Store DNA and note yield
steps.instruction: Store DNA at 4 °C; for long‑term storage keep at –20 °C or –80 °C. Typical yield is 0.2–1 µg per 5 mg fungal sample.
